learning_outcomes.text: Have systematic knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and aspects of both reciprocating and gas turbine internal combustion engines.
Have adequate knowledge of the main elements and processes inherent to internal combustion engines according to current technology and future trends.

Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve problems of determining performance, consumption, and environmental emissions of the engine using established methods in thermal engineering.

Be able to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods in thermal engineering to determine the thermofluid-dynamic operation in the phases of the internal combustion engine cycle, as well as its trends due to changes and control possibilities.
Be able to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs of systems and installations that include internal combustion engines that meet specific performance and behavior requirements.

Understand the different methods in thermal engineering and be able to use them to evaluate the repercussions that design and operational status have on the performance, interaction with the environment, and reliability of internal combustion engines.

Be able to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods to solve problems evaluating the performance and operation of the elements and equipment that integrate an internal combustion engine.
Be able to combine theory and practice of thermodynamics, combustion, fluid flow, heat transfer, and mechanics for solving a specific problem in the field of internal combustion engines.
Understand the applicable methods and techniques in thermal engineering and their limitations when characterizing and designing internal combustion engines.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
Adequate knowledge of their engineering branch, including some knowledge at the forefront of their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to apply their knowledge to develop and carry out designs that meet specific requirements.
Understanding of the different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data and draw conclusions.
Technical and laboratory skills.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
The understanding of methods and techniques applicable and their limitations.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering, to meet with the required specifications.
Applied knowledge of thermal engineering.

syllabus_topics: Internal combustion engines. Classification and applications. Basic processes. Control and performance parameters.
Reciprocating internal combustion engines: Charge renewal process.
Reciprocating internal combustion engines: Filling similarity.
Reciprocating internal combustion engines: Application exercises in filling and similarity.
Reciprocating internal combustion engines: Combustion in spark-ignition engines.
Reciprocating internal combustion engines: Combustion in compression-ignition engines.
Reciprocating internal combustion engines: Variation of performance of reciprocating IC engines with atmospheric conditions. Characteristic curves. Power correction formulas.
Reciprocating internal combustion engines: Application exercises.
Gas turbines: Types of GTs and their applications. Real GT cycles. Component efficiencies. Characteristic curves.
Gas turbines: Operating modes of a GT. Performance and power optimization criteria.
Gas turbines: Variation of GT performance with atmospheric conditions. Characteristic curves. Power correction formulas.
Turbocharging: Energy contained in the exhaust gas. Application technologies in turbocharging.
Pollutant emissions from reciprocating engines and gas turbines. Emission mitigation techniques.

assessment_methods.method: Exercises and/or individual and/or group work
Partial exam of parts of the course

assessment_rules: A final exam will be held to assess the knowledge acquired by the student. A minimum grade will be established for each of the exams and/or parts of the course to pass it. The continuous assessment, weighted at 40%, will be based on exercises, individual/group work, partial exams, and experimental/numerical practices.
